mechanicalProposals.proposals: Explicit fixed anchors; retained shafts and captured keyed accessories; separate pin/arm articulations; complementary finger hinges with rigid stud accessories; reviewed 18942 bottom-beam / 18940 housing sliders with source stop, guide and tooth-end engagement limits
mechanicalProposals.isolation: Read-only analysis; explicit Try creates an unsaved session; separate Save is undoable; no authored placement, inventory or export changes during Play
mechanicalProposals.transmissions: Reviewed external spur and guided rack meshes become ideal coupled relations in the draft
mechanicalProposals.sessionEntry: mechanisms.tryProposal(proposalRequest, playRequest?, physics?): source-bound private Play project; Kinematic or Dynamic; every selected part assigned; unresolved contacts and authored ownership refused
mechanicalProposals.explicitSave: mechanisms.saveProposal(proposalRequest): repeat source-bound review, then undoable rigs.upsert at authored rest pose
mechanicalProposals.reviewInterface: Play settings → Mechanisms: explicit visible assembly or Build selection, fixed parts, groups/joints/relations/ambiguities, one independent motor with bounded speed and effort, Try in Play, separate Save; session controls fit and orbit the whole mechanism

dynamicMechanisms.optIn: play.enter dynamicRigIds (UI: Play > Mechanism physics > Dynamic)
dynamicMechanisms.bodies: One rigid body per authored group; compound convex proxies per member occurrence; anchored groups keep exact triangle surfaces or source-bound reviewed hollow compounds; prismatic bodies on anchored carriers directly retain their constrained world orientation under obstruction, while mobile carriers retain native relative rotation; centered compound children compose position and orientation through the authored frame
dynamicMechanisms.motors: Authored position/velocity motors limited by maxEffort; revolute position targets use accumulated turns with bounded velocity feedback and settled completion; prismatic position targets use bounded force-based velocity feedback with integral load compensation; active low-rate drives stay awake
dynamicMechanisms.vehicles: Rapier ray-cast wheels with sprung suspension, engine force, brake and authored maxSpeed/maxSteer
dynamicMechanisms.pushing: Walking pushes loose bodies with bounded impulses; supported moving bodies carry an upright actor through capsule sweeps, with point velocity on detachment; other contacts do not push the explorer
dynamicMechanisms.reproducibility: Identical reports for identical inputs in the pinned engine/browser; not promised across platforms

mechanicalContacts.status: Verified bounded spur and source-bound 18940/18942 rack drives; fixed and rotating mobile assemblies complete travel/reverse with loads and contact response; measured larger-mechanism ticks exceed a 60 Hz budget and physical-phone throughput remains unverified
mechanicalContacts.policy: Internal contacts remain enabled except rigid welds, declared ideal gear meshes, explicit local revolute bearings, and exact paired reviewed rack floor/cap classes while the entire carrier-relative rack envelope stays aligned; core/end stops, foreign parts and actor contacts retain response
mechanicalContacts.proxies: Reviewed 3700/3701/3702 bores and 3647/3648b source-surface compounds; 18940 housing and 18942 rack use complete source-bound lazy native packets with supplied facets and retained lower-rank support; unbound or changed source refuses before native allocation; smooth 60616a doors retain actual body, pin and handle surfaces in five conservative convex covers; 3582 shutters retain their actual hinge-spine end relief in three source covers
mechanicalContacts.shutterAcceptance: Source-cover opening classification retains only verified travel within existing aggregate contact and sweep caps; both original nested shutters open -60 degrees; real holder and foreign obstacles retain response; exact-rest closing near tangential holder contact can exhaust refinement and remains limited
mechanicalContacts.rackAcceptance: Pinned 24-tooth mount, signed -30 LDU/radian and travel [-88,+10] LDU; forward input150 degrees and reverse slider8 LDU in both modes; native reflected load, stall/retry, authored-frictionless backdrive, angular-momentum and straight/37-degree rotating-carrier checks; source/rest/inventory unchanged; bounded proxy/source precision scope documented; other rack families remain open
mechanicalContacts.kinematicFlatSupport: Complete source-triangle BVH bound to the actual immutable static collider; exact authored Y-axis full-turn or anchored-leaf scalar-interval support certificates; native rounding and all candidate triangles checked within existing work/0.001 LDU guard; changed or unresolved geometry keeps ordinary contact/refinement

transmissions.spur: Ideal external spur relations between parallel revolute shafts on a shared carrier; unwrapped degree positions
transmissions.loadReaction: Angular pinion/shaft and linear rack impulses reflect output resistance to one effort-limited motor and return torque/force to its carrier
transmissions.scope: No tooth contact, backlash, slip, automatic disengagement or certified clutch strength; worm, bevel and differential relations remain pending
transmissions.rack: Ideal signed radius relation between a revolute pinion and limited perpendicular prismatic rack on the same carrier; unwrapped degrees and LDU

closedLinkages.representation: Explicit planar revolute loopClosures separate from acyclic mount joints
closedLinkages.kinematic: Bounded passive-coordinate continuation; supplied poses must already close; ambiguous cold dead centers and unreachable positions refused atomically
closedLinkages.dynamic: Native closure joints transmit load and retain passive travel limits; four-bar, slider-crank and twin-loop steering bench replay verified; steering contact error bounds are load-specific

forceLinks.spring: Authored local attachments, restLengthLdu, stiffnessNewtonsPerMetre and dampingNewtonsSecondsPerMetre; native spring forces and guided travel stops verified
forceLinks.rope: Authored slack-to-taut maximum-length constraint; no winch, routed pulley or visual cable
forceLinks.kinematicPreview: Authored rest retained with explicit Dynamic-only force warning

seatedVehicles.authoring: Explicit chassis-local pelvis/access/approach and 1–4 ordered standing exits; metadata review and undoable save

seatedVehicles.entry: Reach, access ray, supported approach, wheel-envelope clearance and swept raised transfer; refuse before mutation

motors.kinematic: Position motors travel at 90 degrees/s or 40 LDU/s; velocity motors run at their target; swept actor checks block and auto-retry

motors.remoteControls: One usable independent revolute/prismatic motor/joint control at a time; held reverse/forward and proportional speed with release-to-brake; passive transmission and loop coordinates are not editable; rack feedback carries mixed degree/LDU units
motors.overview: Remote controls fit every live group bound into the canvas area clear of the status bar and control sheet; orbit and closer zoom inspect the mechanism, Fit restores the whole system; walking controls are hidden; leaving restores the explorer view; successful seat/train/vehicle context changes switch to the active driving or riding view; refused transitions retain the overview; play.view() reads the rendered camera and overview rig ID

connectedBuilding.name: Snap together
connectedBuilding.kind: UI tool setting (per device, localStorage; not document data)
connectedBuilding.rule: a placement holds when it clashes with nothing and a verified stud, side-stud, jumper or hinge connector mates, or its lowest point is on the ground (y = 0), or (only where connector data is missing on either side) it rests on a part's top; moves are refused only when the moved parts held before and would float or clash after
connectedBuilding.query: connectors.validatePlacement and connectors.validateMove return { ok, via, verified, reason, contacts, targetIds, message }

connectors.snapping: Place previews move to the nearest fit within one stud where the new part makes verified connections (anti-studs on studs, studs in anti-studs), keeping the chosen turn; tapping a face with sideways studs turns the part onto them (spun by Rotate); a door or window pane tapped onto a frame seats closed in its hinge sockets. Fits whose occupancy boxes would pass through another part are refused; otherwise bounds-based stacking
connectors.cycling: Next fit on the placement card (keys N or Tab) cycles the ranked fits; a new tap keeps the previous fit while no other is nearer by more than 6 LDU (hysteresis)
connectors.connectedSelection: Selection tools > Select connected; follows verified stud and hinge connections only
connectors.connectorWorkplane: Workplane and grid > Pick a stud: plane on the stud base, axes follow the part, grid on its stud lattice (side studs included)
connectors.verification: whole-part rules: full-underside, matched-outline, solid-base, jumper, side-studs, partial-underside, hinge-leaf (docs/CONNECTORS.md)

checks.connectivity: exact when every part has verified connectors; approximate when some parts lack them; not-verified when none have them
checks.collisions: approximate (upright catalogue parts, stud rows allowed)

connected-assembly selection through parts without verified connector data
whole-library BFC conformance beyond audited fixtures

buildScripts.cli: brick-cli build --script build.json --output build.mpd [--render view.png --views iso,front] [--target-parts N]
buildScripts.partBudget: --target-parts N / targetParts: guidance, never an error (every component copy counts); the report's target gives parts, difference and percent, costliestOps what made the most; limits.maxParts is the one hard cap (over-budget error, no model written or applied)
buildScripts.oneShot: npm run oneshot -- --target-parts N --brief "…" --model M [--efforts …] [--runner codex|claude]: MineBench-style runs through codex exec or claude -p with no tools; the reply is a brick.build call (JavaScript making the build script, after MineBench's voxel.exec); the curated part list in the prompt (--parts-list), parts search (--search) and up to 3 draft compiles per attempt returning the count and errors (--check) as reply protocols; invalid, overlapping or wrong-colour replies get a repair prompt with the size against the target and the errors; the distance from the target is recorded as a score; searches, checks, finds and part knowledge are recorded
buildScripts.brickBuild: brick-cli build --script build.js (or a JSON file holding {tool: 'brick.build', input: {code}}): code calling one helper per op run once in a Node vm sandbox (10 s, 50,000 ops, 200 KB) in a child process; problems name the code line of their op; --expanded writes the build script; Node only, never in the browser
buildScripts.workspaces: npm run workspace -- --target-parts N[,N…] --brief "…": clean agent directory with the templated prompt and a ./brick-cli that reports every build against the target

partSearch.ranking: roles and builder slang, then curated, commonly produced and connector-verified parts; printed, sticker, Duplo and obsolete variants last
